subject: Follow-up: Starlane call — SLA mapping, topology options, next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@starlane.com>, Marco Tanaka <marco.tanaka@starlane.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Starlane call — SLA mapping, topology options, next steps

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick written recap to make sure we’re aligned and to capture the technical asks so our infra/ops folks can size a concrete test plan.

Summary of pain points you emphasized:
- Production latency spikes during peak campaigns (week-of-release bursts) that cause dropped requests and high retry rates.
- Cost of large-model usage: need to reduce unit cost without materially degrading quality for ranking/creative-assist flows.
- Data residency + audit trail: corporate requirement to keep telemetry in US-only regions and maintain detailed request logs for 30 days.

Stated goals / target SLOs (from today):
- Target p50 latency: <= 250 ms (for 256-token responses).
- Target p95 latency: <= 950 ms (512-token tail acceptable up to ~1.2s for guardrail cases).
- Peak sustained throughput: ~180 qps; burst to 300 qps for <30 minutes during campaign spikes.
- Availability expectation: 99.95% for inference endpoints during business hours (Mon-Fri, 6am-10pm PT).

Technical notes & topology options we discussed:
- Primary plan: Redwood Dedicated pool (US-west region) with reserved capacity + burstable autoscale. Recommend baseline 3xH100-80GB (or equivalent A100-80GB if H100 not available), autoscale to 6 nodes for bursts.
- Multi-variant routing: run a 70B-chat fine-tuned model for quality-critical requests; route lower-priority/auxiliary traffic to a quantized 13B/int8 variant to reduce latency/cost.
- KV/prefix caching: implement 30–45s prefix cache for repeated prompts (campaign templates) and a 30-minute session-level KV cache for streaming dialogs to avoid regen of common prefixes.
- Batching & micro-batching: continuous batching with adaptive windowing to hit throughput targets without bloating p95.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to the 13B quantized model and/or regionally proxied endpoint in case of capacity shortage.
- Telemetry: you’ll share a sample of your production traces so we can simulate token-length distribution and request burst profiles. Marcus will ingest that into the perf model.

Immediate asks / next steps: 
1) Starlane: send a telemetry snippet (sample of requests with timestamps, token lengths, and error types). Elena said you’ll share by EOD today — filename accepted: starlane-telemetry-sample.csv.
2) Redwood: we’ll run a simulated load test against a staging topology (config options below) and produce a sizing + cost delta sheet. Target delivery: initial numbers by Tue (2028-03-06).
3) Schedule ops deep-dive: Marcus to propose 45-min slot next week (look for calendar invite).

Proposed staging topology (we’ll detail in the workbook):
- Baseline: 3xH100 (reserved), model: 70B-chat (fp16), cluster routing with 1x 13B-int8 pool for low-cost fallbacks.
- Autoscale policy: CPU/GPU queue length + latency SLO guardrails; burst to 6 nodes for 20–30 minute windows.
- KV cache TTL: 30 min session cache; prefix cache 45s; eviction LRU.
- Logs: token-level tracing enabled in staging; redact PII by default.

Attachments: we’ll attach a starter sizing workbook and the mutual action plan after the triage run.

Thanks — I’ll follow up after the load run with concrete numbers.

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-9842

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@starlane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Tanaka <marco.tanaka@starlane.com>, Sophie Green <sophie.green@starlane.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Starlane call — SLA mapping, topology options, next steps

Thanks Karthik — this lines up well with what we need. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- Our p95 target is relaxed to 1s for 512-token responses, but we need the p50 to be under 300ms for the majority of UI flows.
- Peak sustained qps for the creative-assist flows is roughly 120 qps; 180 qps was for combined traffic (creative + batch scoring). Expect campaign spikes to push the creative flow to ~220 qps for short periods (10–25 min).
- We require audit logs for 30 days (token-level traces are ok in staging; production should be aggregated traces + request/response hashes to meet compliance).

Attaching a small telemetry sample as promised. It includes timestamps and token counts; sensitive fields redacted.

Attachment: starlane-telemetry-sample.csv (CSV, 32 KB)

I’ll review your proposed sizing once you have the initial numbers. Also looping in Sophie who owns infra budget approvals.

Best,
Elena
Head of ML Products | Starlane Media
elena.ruiz@starlane.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@starlane.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Starlane call — SLA mapping, topology options, next steps

Nice summary — some ops-level notes I’m dropping in so we can be concrete in the workbook: 
- Recommended Dedicated config for stage run: 3xA100-80GB (baseline) with fast autoscale to 6. H100 preferred if available; we’ll present both cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Model mix for tests:
  * Model A: 70B-chat fp16 (quality baseline)
  * Model B: 13B-ggml/int8 (quantized fallback)
- Suggested micro-batching window: dynamic up to 18ms; target effective batch size 8–16 depending on request inter-arrival. This gives throughput headroom without inflating p95.
- KV cache configuration: session-level KV (30 min TTL), prefix cache 45s; for campaign templates we’ll enable pre-warming for scheduled releases.
- Logging & privacy: in staging keep token-level traces; prod: store request/response hash + metadata only. Ops will provide exact retention config for audit logs (30 days) and an export cadence.

Next steps from ops perspective: 
1) Marcus to ingest telemetry CSV and run token-length distribution analysis (ETA EOD Mon).
2) Marcus & I to run a 2-hour soak test targeting combined 200 qps with 10% synthetic campaign bursts to 300 qps. We’ll capture p50/p95/p99 and request failure modes.
3) Post-soak: generate a concise sizing + cost delta (spreadsheet attached).

I attached a starter workbook (redwood-dedicated-config.xlsx) that we’ll fill in as soon as the soak results are available.

--
Monica Patel
Principal Engineer, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@starlane.com>, Sophie Green <sophie.green@starlane.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Starlane call — SLA mapping, topology options, next steps

Thanks all — quick mutual action plan so we’re synced: 
- Starlane (Elena): confirm telemetry sample uploaded to the shared Drive and confirm any additional compliance redaction requirements (due: 2028-03-06 COB).
- Redwood (Marcus & Monica): run the soak + synthetic burst test against the baseline topology, populate redwood-dedicated-config.xlsx with actual p50/p95/p99 numbers, and produce cost delta for 70B vs 13B fallback (due: 2028-03-09).
- Scheduling: Marcus will send a 45-min ops deep-dive invite for Wed or Thu this week to review scaling policies and KV cache tuning.
- Commercial: I’ll open/update the HubSpot deal RDW-2028-019 and drop a preliminary SOW link in the Drive. SOW draft (mutual-action-plan-starlane.docx) will follow once the soak results are in.

If all good I’ll mark the triage run and attach the initial workbook + MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to the soak results.

Regards,
Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
